newsitem.title: CHINA: China urged to curb imports of fibre raw materials.
newsitem.headline: China urged to curb imports of fibre raw materials.

text.p: Industry experts have urged China to curb imports of chemical fibre raw materials to protect the interests of domestic fibre makers, the Economic Information Daily said on Wednesday.
Huge imports of cheap polyester filament and sluggish exports had forced the industry into losses since 1995, the newspaper said.
The domestic share of China's market held by polyester filament firms fell to below 60 percent in 1995 from 87 percent in 1990, it said.
China imported 414,000 tonnes of polyester filament in 1995, compared with 63,000 tonnes in 1990, it said.

Imports of polyester filament in the first half of 1996 were 206,500 tonnes, up 8.8 percent from the same period of 1995 while exports of processed polyester filament goods were 17,000 tonnes, down by 31 percent, it said.
The newspaper said China's chemical fibre industry suffers from a poor economy and over-reliance on imports.
Competition in the domestic market has intensified since a cut in import tariffs last April spurred imports.
